audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 5 and 6 read 'Skill' while the already-audited Sett side gives Sett all seven rows.
audit.why: The two directions must agree; mirror-fix.js would overwrite a disagreement anyway. Sett's base stats, his 16s Facebreaker stun and the unblockable Haymaker centre mean he holds the 1v1 at every stage — Shen's 50.26% comes from Stand United macro, not from lane.
audit.corrected: phases[3]/win[3], phases[5]/win[5], phases[6]/win[6] -> Sett, ratings 5/10 -> 4/10, as matched pairs in one atomic chart group.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] and whys[0] named Sett's passive 'Fists of Steel'. His passive is Pit Grit, and it is not a double-punch — it alternates left and right punches with the right one stronger and faster.
audit.why: Fabricated ability names are the single most damaging defect on these pages, and the described mechanic was wrong as well as the name.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text and whys[0] now use Pit Grit and describe the alternating-punch mechanic; the 'early' paragraph's Pit Grit reference fixed in the same rewrite. Level 3, level 6 and first-item spikes were otherwise correctly placed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields — whys[2], spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and the 'early' paragraph — told you to block Haymaker with Spirit's Refuge. Haymaker is a cast ability, not an attack, so Spirit's Refuge does nothing to it. The page also never mentioned that Facebreaker and The Show Stopper cancel Stand United.
audit.why: Riot's Shen W: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked' — attacks only. Riot's Sett W: 'On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center'. A player following the old text stands in the true-damage centre expecting it to be blocked and dies. Facebreaker stuns (hardCC) and The Show Stopper suppresses, and Stand United is flagged channel/interruptible.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], early, report[5].t and dontsFull[1].d now state the W blanks his autos only and the Haymaker centre must be sidestepped; dontsFull[2].d carries the R-cancel interaction.

audit.why: Haymaker at 18s falling to 12s and Facebreaker at 16s are the two windows that decide when you can commit; Shadow Dash costs 150 energy on an 18s cooldown, which is why chip-dashing loses this lane.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns with Haymaker 18s->12s, Facebreaker 16s and Shadow Dash 18s / 150 energy.

edits.before: Sett's Fists of Steel double-punch and high base stats win the Level 1 stand-off — he can trade you down with no kit commitment before your E is online.
edits.after: Sett's Pit Grit alternating punches and high base stats win the Level 1 stand-off — he can trade you down with no kit commitment before your E is online.

edits.before: W blocks his Haymaker true-damage smash and E forces him to auto your shield down — Sett loses the full-trade exchange if you land the W-block correctly.
edits.after: Haymaker is a spell, so Spirit's Refuge only blanks his autos — deny grit instead: short taunt trades, then step out of the true-damage centre.

edits.before: Sett's Fists of Steel passive double-punch and raw base stats let him win short trades before your W or E are online.
edits.after: Sett's Pit Grit passive makes every right punch stronger and faster, so he wins short trades before your W or E are online.

edits.before: With W and E both up you can block a Haymaker with Spirit's Refuge and taunt Sett into your Q-blade for a full trade — your first real even window.
edits.after: With W and E up you blank his autos with Spirit's Refuge and taunt Sett into your Q-blade — Haymaker still lands, so trade off its 18s cooldown.

edits.before: Use W (Spirit's Refuge) to swallow a Haymaker charge and immediately E-taunt Sett into your empowered autos behind the blade
edits.after: Drop Spirit's Refuge for his autos, then E-taunt Sett into the blade — sidestep the Haymaker centre, W never blocks it

edits.before: Sett's Fists of Steel passive gives him two punches per auto at Level 1 and his base stats are brutally high, so respect his all-in before you have Shadow Dash. Farm with Q at max range and let the spirit blade sit between you — the magic damage it deals through him on Q-empowered autos is free chip he has no reliable answer to. At Level 2 getting E opens short trades: dash, auto, activate Ki Barrier, and leave before his grit bar fills. At Level 3 you have the full trade pattern — but so does Sett. The pivot is your W: when he coils for Haymaker, step your spirit blade in front of you and block the smash, then immediately E-taunt him into your three Q-empowered autos with Ki Barrier absorbing his return. Win the Haymaker cooldown window and reset; lose it and you eat massive true damage.
edits.after: Sett's Pit Grit passive alternates his punches and the right one hits harder and faster, and his base stats are brutally high, so respect his all-in before you have Shadow Dash. Farm with Q at max range and let the spirit blade sit between you — the magic damage it deals through him on Q-empowered autos is free chip he has no reliable answer to. At Level 2 getting E opens short trades: dash, auto, activate Ki Barrier, and leave before his grit bar fills. At Level 3 you have the full trade pattern — but so does Sett. The pivot is grit, not your W: Haymaker is a cast, so Spirit's Refuge blanks his autos and nothing else. Starve the bar with short taunt trades, then walk out of the true-damage centre. Win its 18-second window and reset; stand in it and you eat the lot.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The centre of Haymaker is true damage — armour and MR do nothing.

edits.before: Tunneling the 1v1 while your R could flip a dive bot — Shen who only plays his lane is half a champion.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns and The Show Stopper suppresses — either one cancels Stand United mid-channel.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker: 18s at rank 1 down to 12s — shield plus true damage, and no W blocks it. Bait it, then commit. - Facebreaker: 16s, his stun. - Shadow Dash: 18s, 150 energy — never spend it on chip.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: Shield + true damage. Bait it. When it is down — E-Q + R him.
edits.after: Haymaker is a spell — Spirit's Refuge blanks his autos, never the true-damage punch.

notes: Chart conflict: the packet levelChart for this matchup reads Sett / Skill / Skill / Skill / Shen / Shen / Skill, but the already-audited Sett side set all seven rows to Sett. I followed the mirror because the two directions must not contradict and mirror-fix.js would overwrite me otherwise — but a reviewer should decide which source is authoritative here, since a 50.26% Shen win rate with Sett winning every stage is a strange page. Not asserted anywhere because the kits do not say it: whether Facebreaker's pull can drag Shen out of his own Spirit's Refuge zone, and whether tenacity shortens his stun enough to matter.
